title: The Blind Spot of Agent Safety: How Benign User Instructions Expose Critical Vulnerabilities in Computer-Use Agents
notes: Introduces OS-Blind, a 300-task benchmark evaluating computer-use agents under benign-instruction/unintended-harm conditions. Contributes a test set and measurements, no new named attack or defense.

title: Security Engineering of OpenClaw: Analyzing Attack Surface Expansion and Trust-Boundary Violations
notes: Quantitative measurement study of OpenClaw under prompt injection, reporting metrics (attack-surface entropy, privilege drift, escalation curvature) and testing generic controls (policy gating, execution filtering). Metrics are named, but no new attack or defense technique is.

title: Cross-layer contagion of prompt injections in multi-agent swarms: a multiplex microscopic markov chain approach
notes: Formal epidemic-style model (coupled multiplex MMCA with SEIQ-SIS dynamics) of how prompt injection spreads through shared MCP tools. The named contribution is an analytical model plus a budget-allocation rule, not an attack or defense technique.

title: LLM Agent Honeypot: Monitoring AI Hacking Agents in the Wild
notes: Deploys an SSH honeypot instrumented with prompt injection and timing probes to identify autonomous LLM attackers in the wild. The named system detects attacking agents, not poisoned context, so it is out of scope for RQ4.

title: The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents
notes: White-box security analysis of Browser Use with a CVE and PoC; recommends a defense-in-depth stack of off-the-shelf parts (input sanitization, planner-executor isolation, formal analyzers, session safeguards) without naming a new method.

title: Evaluating Privilege Usage of Agents with Real-World Tools
notes: Proposes GrantBox, a sandbox that wires real-world tools to agents to measure privilege usage under prompt injection. An evaluation harness, not a technique.

title: LOCA-bench: Benchmarking Language Agents Under Controllable and Extreme Context Growth
notes: Benchmark that controls agent context growth to measure context-rot style degradation; evaluates existing context-management scaffolds rather than proposing one.

title: Positional Failures in Long-Context LLMs: A Blind Spot in Reasoning Benchmarks
notes: Audits 11 long-context benchmarks and proposes Context Rot Evaluation (CRE), a position-controlled evaluation protocol. The phenomenon studied (positional sensitivity / lost-in-the-middle) is pre-existing, and the paper explicitly says its duplicate-at-end probe is a diagnostic, not a mitigation.

title: Context Cartography: Toward Structured Governance of Contextual Space in Large Language Models
notes: Conceptual framework mapping context into zones and seven cartographic operators, then showing four existing systems already implement them. Systematises converging practice it did not invent; no new technique.

title: GPT-5 vs Other LLMs in Long Short-Context Performance
notes: Empirical comparison of four models on long-input tasks; reports degradation past 70K tokens and argues lost-in-the-middle is largely resolved in newer models. Measurement only.

title: Understanding Parametric Knowledge Injection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: Analysis of parametric RAG (P-RAG) versus token RAG, including robustness to retrieval noise and knowledge conflict. Studies an existing paradigm; the PT-RAG combination is an ablation setting, not a poisoning defense.

title: Beyond Isolated Capabilities: Bridging Long CoT Reasoning and Long-Context Understanding
notes: Studies whether reasoning distillation from DeepSeek-R1 improves long-context multi-document QA and mitigates lost-in-the-middle. Applies off-the-shelf distillation; no named technique.

title: LongFuncEval: Measuring the effectiveness of long context models for function calling
notes: Evaluation suite measuring degradation from large tool catalogs, long tool responses and long multi-turn histories. Benchmark only.

title: Attribute or Abstain: Large Language Models as Long Document Assistants
notes: Presents LAB, a benchmark of six long-document attribution tasks, and compares existing attribution approaches. Benchmark only; finds no lost-in-the-middle effect for attribution.

title: CUB: Benchmarking Context Utilisation Techniques for Language Models
notes: Benchmark comparing seven existing context-utilisation manipulation techniques under noisy RAG contexts; contributes an evaluation suite and a utilisation metric, not a technique.

title: OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows
notes: Long-horizon office-workflow benchmark plus HomerAgents, a multi-agent pipeline for generating benchmark tasks. Both are evaluation infrastructure.

title: Can We Rely on LLM Agents to Draft Long-Horizon Plans? Let's Take TravelPlanner as an Example
notes: Failure study on TravelPlanner proposing Feedback-Aware Fine-Tuning (FAFT) for plan quality and a per-task 'Scrubber' filtration agent for lengthy noisy context. Borderline: the Scrubber is named but is ordinary task-specific context filtering, and FAFT targets planning accuracy rather than context integrity.

title: AMemGym: Interactive Memory Benchmarking for Assistants in Long-Horizon Conversations
notes: Interactive on-policy environment for evaluating conversational memory systems; contributes structured data sampling, simulated users and memory metrics. Evaluation infrastructure only.

title: LPS-Bench: Benchmarking Safety Awareness of Computer-Use Agents in Long-Horizon Planning under Benign and Adversarial Scenarios
notes: Planning-time safety benchmark for MCP-based computer-use agents. Its mitigations are off-the-shelf prompt-based ones (human-in-the-loop clarification, safety prompting), not new named defenses.

title: MemGym: a Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
notes: Unifies existing agent gyms behind one memory-reasoning interface and trains MemRM, a small reward model used as a cheap evaluator. Benchmark plus evaluation tooling.

title: LUMINA: Long-horizon Understanding for Multi-turn Interactive Agents
notes: Procedurally generated multi-turn environments plus an oracle-intervention framework that ablates planning, state tracking and history pruning to find capability bottlenecks. Diagnostic study, no named technique.

title: Do Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Adapt to Varying User Needs?
notes: Evaluation framework crossing three user-need cases with three context settings (match, knowledge conflict, irrelevant) plus the URAQ dataset. Measures behaviour under conflicting context rather than proposing a method.

title: On the Inseparability of Instructions and Data in Shared-Embedding Sequence Models
notes: Theory paper proving that perfect prompt-injection prevention is impossible inside a shared representational pipeline. Semantic-Faithful Control is a named security property/goal, not a defense mechanism.

title: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
notes: StakeBench reframes prompt-injection evaluation for web agents around which stakeholder bears the harm. Benchmark only.

title: The Surface You Test Is Not the Surface That Breaks
notes: Holds an injection payload byte-identical and delivers it via tool output (data surface) versus tool description (schema surface), reporting an Adaptive Attack Rate. The schema channel is pre-existing tool-metadata injection; the contribution is a cross-surface evaluation design and metric.

title: The Convergent Cyber Threat Horizon in Financial Services: Artificial Intelligence, Agentic Systems, Deepfakes, Quantum Computing, and the Mythos of Large Language Models
notes: Sector position paper offering a five-vector threat taxonomy, a seven-domain defence framework mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 and DORA, and a preparedness roadmap. Taxonomy and policy, no technique.

title: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detection for Web Agents
notes: Open-source benchmarking framework with a 5,000-prompt labelled dataset and a modular detector harness comparing existing detection methods. Benchmark only.

title: The Evolution of Tool Use in LLM Agents: From Single-Tool Call to Multi-Tool Orchestration
notes: Survey of multi-tool agent literature organised around six dimensions, including safety and control. Survey, excluded by definition.

title: From Assistant to Double Agent: Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks on OpenClaw for Personalized Local AI Agent
notes: PASB is an end-to-end security benchmark for personalized agents; it explicitly reuses existing attack paradigms (combined IPI, memory poisoning) and existing defenses (delimiter, sandwich) and measures them on OpenClaw.

title: FinVault: Benchmarking Financial Agent Safety in Execution-Grounded Environments
notes: Execution-grounded financial-agent security benchmark with 31 sandbox scenarios and 963 test cases drawn from regulatory violation patterns. Contributes an attack taxonomy and test suite, not a technique.

title: Penetration Testing of Agentic AI: A Comparative Security Analysis Across Models and Frameworks
notes: Comparative penetration test of five models on AutoGen and CrewAI over 13 attack scenarios. Coins 'hallucinated compliance' for a defensive behaviour pattern where models fabricate outputs instead of refusing or complying, but that is an observed model behaviour, not an attack or defense technique.

title: Enhancing Security in LLM Applications: A Performance Evaluation of Early Detection Systems
notes: Comparative evaluation of three existing open-source prompt-injection detectors (LLM Guard, Vigil, Rebuff), finding their canary-word checks ineffective and proposing configuration fixes. Improvements to existing tools, not a new named defense.

title: Small Models, Big Tasks: An Exploratory Empirical Study on Small Language Models for Function Calling
notes: Empirical comparison of small language models on function calling with five new evaluation metrics. Capability study, no security or context-integrity technique.

title: Whispers in the Machine: Confidentiality in Agentic Systems
notes: Formalizes agent confidentiality via a secret-string abstraction and evaluates ten agents against fourteen attack strategies adapted from prior work plus five existing defenses. Formalization and evaluation, explicitly adapted attacks.

title: GateMem: Benchmarking Memory Governance in Multi-Principal Shared-Memory Agents
notes: Benchmark for multi-principal shared memory covering utility, access control and active forgetting. Evaluates existing memory baselines; no proposed governance mechanism.

title: Overeager Coding Agents: Measuring Out-of-Scope Actions on Benign Tasks
notes: Coins 'overeager actions' for out-of-scope agent behaviour on benign prompts and builds OverEager-Gen to measure it. The paper explicitly distinguishes this from prompt injection; it is an authorization failure mode, not a context-poisoning mechanism or context-degradation effect.

title: HarmfulSkillBench: How Do Harmful Skills Weaponize Your Agents?
notes: Large-scale measurement of 98,440 published agent skills plus a benchmark showing pre-installed harmful skills lower refusal rates. Measurement and benchmark; harmful skills are misuse artifacts, not a named technique.

title: Risky-Bench: Probing Agentic Safety Risks under Real-World Deployment
notes: Principle-driven safety evaluation pipeline that derives context-aware rubrics and applies them to life-assist agents. Benchmark framework only.

title: MLA-Trust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of Multimodal LLM Agents in GUI Environments
notes: Unified trustworthiness benchmark for GUI agents across truthfulness, controllability, safety and privacy with 34 tasks. Benchmark only.

title: ToLeaP: Rethinking Development of Tool Learning with Large Language Models
notes: Reproduces 33 tool-learning benchmarks on 41 LLMs as a unified platform and analyses 3,000 failure cases. Platform plus analysis; directions are sketched, not named methods.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
notes: Reproducible web environment with functional websites and functional-correctness tasks for agent evaluation. The canonical benchmark environment, no technique.

title: Toward Secure LLM Agents: Threat Surfaces, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation
notes: Survey synthesizing 247 papers under a lifecycle-based framework of information flow, delegated authority and persistent state. Survey, excluded by definition.

title: TraceSafe: A Systematic Assessment of LLM Guardrails on Multi-Step Tool-Calling Trajectories
notes: TraceSafe-Bench evaluates 13 LLM-as-a-guard models and 7 existing guardrails on mid-trajectory risk detection across 12 risk categories. Evaluates other people's defenses.

title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations
notes: Reformulates conversational memory as lifecycle operations (remember, forget, update, reflect) with gold operation traces for operation-level diagnosis. Benchmark and formulation, no technique.

title: LongMedBench: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Long-Horizon Clinical Decision-Making
notes: MIMIC-IV-derived benchmark for long-horizon clinical agents with three evaluation suites; evaluates existing RAG and memory systems (e.g. Mem0). Benchmark only.

title: Benchmarking Serverless AI Architectures: Modular RAG, Serverless RAG, and Long Context Inference
name: Context Fatigue
evidence_quote: our paper formally defines and addresses a phenomenon we call “Context Fatigue”. When processing massive documents (e.g., 300 pages), the LLM experiences severe data overload in the final phases of a prolonged session.
notes: Primarily a cost/latency/accuracy comparison of three serverless RAG and long-context architectures, but it explicitly coins and defines 'Context Fatigue' for degradation late in a prolonged session over very large documents. CAUTION: this is plausibly a renaming of context rot / long-context accumulation degradation rather than a distinct mechanism, and the paper is a venue-light benchmarking study.

title: External Experience Serving in Production LLM Systems: A Deployment-Oriented Study of Quality-Cost Trade-offs
notes: Production study comparing no-experience, random, global-injection and retrieval-based selective injection of reusable operational experience on quality versus serving cost. The coined term 'serving-interface break-even' is an economic operating point, not a technique.

title: Can It Reach the Generator? Investigating the Survival of Prompt-Injection Attacks in Realistic RAG Settings
notes: Re-evaluates seven existing GEO prompt-injection attacks through a full retriever-reranker-generator pipeline and shows most collapse before reaching the generator. The detector is an off-the-shelf guard finetuned on a small dataset, matching the batch-1 exclusion for applied classifiers.
